name: Sanctions & coercion
value: France seeks EU Iran cyber curbs; US Cuba list
summary: France blamed an IRGC cyber unit for supermarket attacks and seeks EU sanctions; US named Cuba and China targets 5 Nov
state: Paris prosecutors said on 9 Nov that an IRGC-linked cyber unit was behind the 12 Oct attack on refrigeration in about 700 supermarkets; France summoned Iran's ambassador and will seek EU sanctions (AP via The Manila Times, 11 Nov). On 5 Nov the US State Department designated eight entities, including two China-based suppliers to Cuba's military, two individuals and five vessels. The EU's next Russia package is still expected. No major economy has been cut off from payment systems and no large sovereign-asset seizure was found as of 12 Nov.
for_you: Firms trading with Iran, Russia, Cuba or listed Chinese suppliers face compliance exposure. UK businesses can check OFSI guidance on GOV.UK for current UK sanctions lists.
rubric_hit: Major new packages or threats (Watch): EU Iran cyber sanctions sought, US Cuba designations; no payment cut-off or sovereign seizure

sources.title: The Manila Times (AP) — France blames Iran for cyberattack on supermarkets
US State Department — Further sanctions on the Cuban regime's foreign military support and illicit revenue networks

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
drivers: Russia/Iran sanctions packages, secondary sanctions, frozen-asset decisions, export controls.
